judge_assessment.explanation: The judge's central claim is correct and I verified it the hard way, recomputing each figure from its tikz vertex list rather than from the labels: 8x3+4x3=36; 10+4+5+3+5+7=34; 9x3+5x4=47; 4+4+2+3+8+3+2+4=30; 10x6-3x2=54; 12-5=7; 12x5+5x3=75; 15x10-4x6=126; 16+5+9+7+7+12=56; 13-5=8; 12x9-4x3=96 (the unlabelled right-hand vertical being 9-6=3); and the staircase 12x3+8x3+4x3=72. All twelve match verify.json and the key, and every drawn polygon is consistent with every label on it. 'Dimensions are unambiguous' is true to a reader. It is not true to the gate: gate_log.txt step 20 reports 'Figure-label numbers not found in JSON givens' for 9 of 12 problems, and the JSON tries to silence it by padding 'at' with variables the expr never uses — the exact bypass check_prose_consistency.py documents and filters out. So a third of the sheet's printed dimensions are correct but unverified, and the build shipped with nine unresolved warnings.

strengths_to_preserve: The two challenge problems are properly built rather than merely bigger. Problem 11 leaves the right-hand vertical unlabelled so the student must derive 9 - 6 = 3 before subtracting the corner, and problem 12 is a three-step staircase whose dashed decomposition lines show three flat rectangles (12x3, 8x3, 4x3) — the stem names the cut explicitly ('three rectangles that each lie flat like a step'), so the challenge is the arithmetic rather than guessing the intended decomposition.

\figsplit puts each figure in a 0.40-width minipage beside its own 0.56-width work space, so no problem can borrow a neighbour's figure and every diagram sits next to the space where its work goes; the layout gate confirms all 12 problems clear the work-space floor.

Every answer line carries its unit via \answerline{cm$^2$} / \answerline{ft} and the JSON declares the matching answer_unit, so the area-versus-perimeter confusion this topic reliably produces is caught at the point where the student writes the answer rather than after.

Problems 5 and 8 draw the missing corner as a dashed rectangle, which makes 'whole minus corner' something the student can see; the key then reconciles the two methods so decomposition and subtraction are presented as interchangeable rather than as separate procedures.

root_causes.description: Composite rectilinear figures print more side lengths than any single area or perimeter expression consumes — the redundant sides are exactly what makes the figure readable and what a student uses to derive a missing length. The generator responded to the figure-label audit by adding those lengths to 'at' as variables the expr never references (m, n), which check_prose_consistency.py explicitly filters as a one-field way to silence the gate. The result is a sheet where a third of the printed dimensions carry no check at all, and nine warnings that a reader learns to scroll past.
evidence: verify.json id 1: at {a: 8, b: 3, c: 4, h: 3, m: 6} for expr 'a*b + c*h' — 'm' is never referenced, and the figure's left side is labelled 6.
verify.json ids 7 and 11 add both 'm' and 'n' as unused keys; verify_study_guide.json does the same (id 1 has m: 5, id 2 has m: 3 and n: 6).
gate_log.txt step 20: 'Figure-label numbers not found in JSON givens (audit 3d)' listing problems 1, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10, 11 and 12 — nine of twelve.

tests/check_prose_consistency.py json_numbers(): 'An `at` binding the expression never uses is not a verified given ... Walking all of `at` made it a one-field way to silence this gate.' The bypass is anticipated and defeated, so the padding buys nothing.
The affected labels are load-bearing for the student: problem 6's 2, 4 and 6 are what justify the missing side, and problem 10's 4, 6 and 10 likewise.

improvements.title: Redundant composite-figure side labels are padded into 'at' instead of verified
improvements.proposed_change: Say plainly in SKILL.md that padding 'at' with keys the expr never uses does not satisfy the figure-label audit and must not be used for that purpose, and give the supported route instead: add a real check for each redundant label under the same problem id — for problem 1, eval('b + h') expected 6 for the left side; for problem 6, eval('4 + 2') expected 6; for problem 12, eval('3 + 3 + 3') expected 9. These are one-line entries and they encode the very relation the figure depends on (opposite sides of a rectilinear figure must sum). Then make check_prose_consistency.py's figure-label report name that supported fix in its message, and have verify.py warn at exit 2 when an 'at' dict carries keys absent from the expr, so the bypass is refused loudly where it is written rather than silently filtered three gates later.
improvements.regression_test: Two assertions. (1) verify.py fixture: an entry with expr 'a*b + c*h' and at {a: 8, b: 3, c: 4, h: 3, m: 6} must exit 2 naming the unused key 'm'; the same entry without 'm' must exit 0. (2) check_prose_consistency.py fixture: curr-095's worksheet problem 1 block paired with a verify JSON that adds eval('b + h') expected 6 under id 1 must report 'Figure labels: all consistent with JSON givens', while the currently shipped padded JSON must still report the warning. Today assertion (1) fails outright (no such warning exists) and (2) fails on its first half.
improvements.expected_impact: Every printed dimension on a composite-figure sheet becomes machine-checked, which is what the audit-3d gate was built for. It also removes the incentive to pad 'at', so the nine-warning tail disappears instead of being normalised, and the redundant-side relations students actually use to find missing lengths get verified for the first time.
improvements.risk: Rejecting unused 'at' keys outright would invalidate existing documents — the checker's own comment records five tasks carrying innocent unused keys — so this must be a warning (exit 2) rather than a hard failure, and the message must name the supported alternative or authors will simply delete the key and leave the label unverified.

case_summary: Twelve composite rectilinear problems that are mathematically flawless — I recomputed each one from its tikz vertex list, including the derived side in problem 11 and the three-step staircase in problem 12, and every label on every polygon is consistent. Layout, unit binding and figure scope are all handled well. The gap is verification coverage of the figures themselves: nine of twelve problems print side lengths that no check covers, and the JSON pads 'at' with unused variables in an attempt to quiet the audit — a bypass the checker anticipates and filters, so the build shipped with nine unresolved figure-label warnings.
